authoredSolutions.51: \(f\) is strictly increasing on \([1,\infty)\), so \(f(x)=f^{-1}(x)\iff f(x)=x\): \((x-1)^4+1=x\Rightarrow(x-1)^4=(x-1)\Rightarrow x=1,2\), exactly two elements, so (I) is TRUE. For (II), \(f(x)=f^{-1}(x+1)\Rightarrow f(f(x))=x+1\Rightarrow(x-1)^{16}+1=x+1\Rightarrow(x-1)^{16}=x\), which has a root in \((2,3)\), so \(S\) is non-empty and (II) is FALSE. Only (I) is TRUE. Answer: (A).
authoredSolutions.53: Subtracting the first equation: \(R_2-R_1:(0,1,2\mid 4)\) and \(R_3-R_1:(0,2,\lambda-1\mid\mu-5)\). Infinitely many solutions need \(R_3-R_1=2(R_2-R_1)\): \(\lambda-1=4,\ \mu-5=8\), so \(\lambda=5,\ \mu=13\). Hence \(\lambda+\mu=18\). Answer: (B).
authoredSolutions.54: Real coefficients force the third root \(1-i\sqrt2\). Then \(x^3+ax^2+bx+c=(x-1)(x^2-2x+3)=x^3-3x^2+5x-3\), so \(a=-3,b=5,c=-3\). In \(\int_{-1}^{1}(x^3-3x^2+5x-3)\,dx\) the odd terms vanish, giving \(-3\cdot\tfrac23-3\cdot2=-2-6=-8\). Answer: (C).
authoredSolutions.55: Discriminant \(\ge 0\): \(9\lambda^2-16\lambda(\lambda+2)\ge0\Rightarrow-\tfrac{32}{7}\le\lambda\le0\). Sum \(\tfrac{3\lambda}{\lambda+2}>0\) and product \(\tfrac{4\lambda}{\lambda+2}>0\) both require \(\lambda<-2\) or \(\lambda>0\). Intersection: \(-\tfrac{32}{7}\le\lambda<-2\). Integers \(\lambda=-4,-3\), i.e. \(2\) values. Answer: (B).
authoredSolutions.56: \(\det(A-\alpha I)=0\Rightarrow\alpha^3+8\alpha^2-88\alpha-320=0=(\alpha-8)(\alpha^2+16\alpha+40)\), roots \(8,\ -8\pm2\sqrt6\); largest \(p=8\). Circle \((x-8)^2+(y-16)^2=320\). On \(y=0\): \((x-8)^2=64\Rightarrow x=0,16\); on \(x=0\): \((y-16)^2=256\Rightarrow y=0,32\). Distinct points \((0,0),(16,0),(0,32)\): \(3\) points. Answer: (C).
authoredSolutions.58: \(\sum(x_i+2)^2-\sum(x_i-1)^2=6\sum x_i+30=90\Rightarrow\sum x_i=10\), mean \(=1\). From \(\sum(x_i-1)^2=\sum x_i^2-2\sum x_i+10=90\), \(\sum x_i^2=100\). Variance \(=\tfrac{100}{10}-1^2=9\), so SD \(=3\). Answer: (D).
authoredSolutions.59: \(T_{r+1}=\binom{18}{r}(9x)^{18-r}\left(-\tfrac{1}{3\sqrt x}\right)^r\); the power of \(x\) is \(18-\tfrac{3r}{2}=0\Rightarrow r=12\). Coefficient \(=\binom{18}{12}9^{6}3^{-12}=\binom{18}{6}\cdot\tfrac{3^{12}}{3^{12}}=18564\). So \(221k=18564\Rightarrow k=84\). Answer: (A).
authoredSolutions.60: Circle has centre \((7,7)\), radius \(4\). Matching centroid coordinates: \(Q_x+R_x=6,\ Q_y+R_y=9\); with \(R_x+R_y=5\) this gives \(Q_x+Q_y=10\). Intersecting \(x+y=10\) with the circle: \(Q_x=3,7\Rightarrow Q_y=7,3\). Then \(R_y=9-Q_y=2,6\), sum \(=8\). Answer: (D).
authoredSolutions.61: \(2c=6\Rightarrow c=3\); \(\tfrac{2a}{e}=\tfrac83\) with \(e=\tfrac3a\) gives \(\tfrac{a^2}{3}=\tfrac43\Rightarrow a^2=4\), \(b^2=c^2-a^2=5\). On \(x=\alpha\): \(y^2=5\!\left(\tfrac{\alpha^2}{4}-1\right)\), area \(=|\alpha|\sqrt{5\!\left(\tfrac{\alpha^2}{4}-1\right)}=4\sqrt{15}\). Squaring: \(\left(\tfrac{\alpha^2}{4}-1\right)\alpha^2=48\Rightarrow\alpha^4-4\alpha^2-192=0\Rightarrow\alpha^2=16\). Answer: (B).
authoredSolutions.62: Let \(t=\tfrac x2\) and maximize \(16\sin t\cos^3 t\) on \([0,\tfrac\pi2]\). The derivative \(\propto\cos^2 t\,(\cos^2 t-3\sin^2 t)=0\Rightarrow\tan^2 t=\tfrac13,\ t=\tfrac\pi6\). Value \(=16\cdot\tfrac12\cdot\left(\tfrac{\sqrt3}{2}\right)^3=16\cdot\tfrac{3\sqrt3}{16}=3\sqrt3\). Answer: (B).
authoredSolutions.64: Let \(P=(\alpha,2\alpha,1)\) with image \(P'\). The segment \(PP'\perp(3,2,1)\): \(3(\alpha+1)+2(\alpha^2-5\alpha)+\tfrac{\alpha-3}{2}=0\Rightarrow4\alpha^2-13\alpha+3=0\Rightarrow\alpha=3,\tfrac14\). The midpoint must lie on the line; checking, only \(\alpha=3\) is consistent with \(x=2+3t\) (\(\alpha=\tfrac14\) fails). Answer: (A).
authoredSolutions.65: \(|\hat u\times\hat v|=\sin\theta=\tfrac{\sqrt3}{2}\Rightarrow\theta=60^\circ,\ \cos\theta=\tfrac12\). Dotting \(\vec A=\lambda\hat u+\hat v+(\hat u\times\hat v)\): \(\vec A\cdot\hat u=\lambda+\tfrac12\) and \(\vec A\cdot\hat v=\tfrac\lambda2+1\). Eliminating constants gives \(\lambda=\tfrac43(\vec A\cdot\hat u)-\tfrac23(\vec A\cdot\hat v)\). Answer: (A).
authoredSolutions.66: Put \(x=0\): \(f(y)=f(0)+2y^2+y=2y^2+y-1\). Matching the \(\alpha xy\) term in the functional equation forces \(\alpha=4\). Then \(\sum_{n=1}^5(\alpha+f(n))=\sum_{n=1}^5(2n^2+n+3)=2(55)+15+15=140\). Answer: (B).
authoredSolutions.67: For each \(c=0,1,\dots,11\), \(a+b=22-2c\) has \(23-2c\) non-negative integer solutions. \(\sum_{c=0}^{11}(23-2c)=12\cdot23-2\cdot66=276-132=144\). Answer: (C).
authoredSolutions.68: The curves \(x=-3y^2\) and \(x=1-4y^2\) meet where \(-3y^2=1-4y^2\Rightarrow y=\pm1\). The horizontal width is \((1-4y^2)-(-3y^2)=1-y^2\). Area \(=\int_{-1}^{1}(1-y^2)\,dy=2\left(1-\tfrac13\right)=\tfrac43\). Answer: (C).
authoredSolutions.69: The coefficient of \(y\) equals \(\dfrac{d}{dx}\ln\dfrac{x^3+2}{2+e^{-2x}}\), so the integrating factor is \(\dfrac{x^3+2}{2+e^{-2x}}\). Then \(\dfrac{d}{dx}\!\left(y\cdot\text{IF}\right)=x^3+2\Rightarrow y\cdot\dfrac{x^3+2}{2+e^{-2x}}=\dfrac{x^4}{4}+2x+C\). \(y(0)=\tfrac32\Rightarrow C=1\). At \(x=1\): \(\dfrac{3y}{2+e^{-2}}=\tfrac{13}{4}\Rightarrow y=\tfrac{13}{12}(2+e^{-2})\), so \(\alpha=\tfrac{13}{12}\). Answer: (D).
authoredSolutions.71: Total \(=\binom{31}{3}=4495\). Increasing 3-term APs: for common difference \(d\) there are \(31-2d\) choices, so \(\sum_{d=1}^{15}(31-2d)=465-240=225\). Probability \(=\dfrac{225}{4495}=\dfrac{45}{899}\) with \(\gcd=1\). Hence \(a+b=45+899=944\). Answer: 944.
authoredSolutions.72: \(f(|x|)=x^2-5|x|+6\) is continuous everywhere, non-differentiable only at \(x=0\). Since \(f\) jumps at \(0\) (\(e^{-1}\) vs \(6\)), \(|f(x)|\) and hence \(g\) is discontinuous at \(x=0\): \(\alpha=1\). \(|f(x)|=|(x-2)(x-3)|\) gives corners at \(x=2,3\); together with \(x=0\), \(g\) is non-differentiable at \(0,2,3\): \(\beta=3\). \(\alpha+\beta=4\). Answer: 4.
authoredSolutions.73: The half-lines \(x-\sqrt3\,y=\alpha\ (y>0)\) and \(x+\sqrt3\,y=\alpha\ (y<0)\) meet at \((\alpha,0)\), each making \(30^\circ\) with the bisector (x-axis), so they enclose \(60^\circ\). Taking \(A,B\) symmetric at perpendicular distance \(\alpha\) from the bisector gives \(QA=QB=AB=2\alpha\). Using \(PQ=\tfrac92\) with the circumradius \(R\) of \(\triangle PAB\) via the sine rule yields \(\dfrac{\alpha^2}{R}=9\). Answer: 9.
authoredSolutions.74: Write points as \((4t^2,8t)\); \(B\) is \(t=1\). The slope joining \(t_i,t_j\) is \(\tfrac{2}{t_i+t_j}\); the right angle at \(B\) gives \(\tfrac{2}{1+t_1}\cdot\tfrac{2}{1+t_2}=-1\Rightarrow t_1+t_2+t_1t_2=-5\). For the centroid \((X,Y)\) with \(s=t_1+t_2,\ p=t_1t_2\), eliminating yields \(9Y^2=48X-640\), i.e. \(Y^2=\tfrac{16}{3}\!\left(X-\tfrac{40}{3}\right)\). Latus rectum \(=\tfrac{16}{3}\); three times \(=16\). Answer: 16.
authoredSolutions.75: \(\int_0^x\tan(t-x)\,dt=\ln\cos x\), so \(f(x)=\ln\cos x-\int_0^x f(t)\tan t\,dt\). Differentiating: \(f'(x)=-\tan x\,(1+f(x))\) with \(f(0)=0\). Solving gives \(1+f=\cos x\Rightarrow f(x)=\cos x-1\). Then \(f''=-\cos x,\ f'=-\sin x\): \(f''(\tfrac\pi6)+12f'(-\tfrac\pi6)+f(\tfrac\pi6)=-\tfrac{\sqrt3}{2}+12\cdot\tfrac12+(\tfrac{\sqrt3}{2}-1)=5\). Answer: 5.
